record_identity.title: Technically available access mistaken for cross-organisational authority

summary: A prospective failure mode in which an AI agent, operator, harness, or receiving organisation treats technically successful access through residual, inherited, shared, mistakenly retained, or exploitable credentials as authority to act across another organisation's boundary. The ongoing Apple–OpenAI trade-secret litigation is disputed motivating context only; this record does not assert that an OpenAI agent accessed Apple systems or information.
why_it_matters_to_CAM: Technical access can become unauthorised invocation, acquisition, exfiltration, and downstream use at machine speed. Responsibility must remain non-offsetting: a source organisation's access-control failure does not authorise another actor's use, and unauthorised use does not erase the source organisation's responsibility for the exploitable condition.

contextual_relations.rationale: FM-0044 governs unauthorised instrumental pathways; FM-0056 governs the cross-organisational authority and custody chain.
FM-0054 concerns real targets mistaken for simulation scope; FM-0056 applies where technical access is mistaken for permission.
Monitoring failure can amplify but does not replace the underlying authority breach.

failure_mode_definition: Technical reachability, credential validity, exploitability, residual access, inherited access, authentication success, prior employment, or contextual familiarity is treated as authority to act across an organisational or custodial boundary without independently validated authorisation for the actor, target, action, scope, purpose, and effective period. The chain may continue through acquisition, exfiltration, custody transfer, retention, propagation, analysis, training, or product use.
failure_threshold: The threshold is met when a consequential cross-boundary target action occurs without validated authority even though access technically succeeds. Discovery may be a warning condition; unauthorised invocation, opening or transforming protected information, copying or exporting it, and retaining or using it are escalating completed stages. Malicious intent is not required.

failure_classification.likelihood: plausible and increasing with broad agent tool access and enterprise integration
failure_classification.confidence: high for the general mechanism; no claim of AI-agent involvement in the motivating litigation
failure_classification.failure_scope: agent / operator / identity layer / source organisation / receiving organisation / downstream systems
failure_classification.recurrence_pattern: May recur when agents inherit human credentials, reuse sessions, traverse collaboration boundaries, or ingest protected information without target-specific authority and provenance.
failure_classification.taxonomy_reference: CAM-EQ2026-OPERATIONS-003-SUP-01 Appendix B — OPS.FF.SECURITY-INTEGRITY; VIGIL subtype: technically-available-access-mistaken-for-cross-organisational-authority
failure_classification.persistence: Persists until authority is validated, access is constrained, acquired material is traced and contained, downstream uses are identified, and responsibilities are separately actioned.
failure_classification.reproducibility: Test with residual-session, former-employee, shared-device, inherited-token, changed-target, changed-purpose, and downstream-custody scenarios.
failure_classification.visibility: Often low because logs may show valid authentication while legal and governance authority is absent.

cam_internal.governance_layer: cross-organisational authority / credentials / acquisition and exfiltration / downstream custody / incident attribution
cam_internal.routing_note: SECURITY owns the boundary doctrine. OPERATIONS retains incident lifecycle, evidence custody, response, recovery, and legal-regulatory interface. Annex B needs only structural formation and authority fields.
cam_internal.validator_or_automation_impact: possible future authority-tuple, quarantine, and provenance checks

ecosystem_status.basis: Residual credentials and unauthorised access are established cybersecurity risks; the AI-agent chain is prospective and the Apple–OpenAI litigation remains disputed.

repair_status.verification_note: No adopted CAM amendment or external conformance evidence establishes the complete control.

corpus_coverage.coverage_summary: SECURITY-001 and SECURITY-002 already distinguish access, exploitability, credential possession, retrieval, contextual presence, and successful execution from authority. OPERATIONS already covers incident lifecycle and evidence. The remaining gap is an explicit cross-organisational residual-credential, non-offsetting attribution, and downstream custody rule.

sections: Access and successful execution are not authority
Review on target or credential change
Retrieval and contextual presence do not create execution authority
Incident intake, containment, response, and recovery
